description:
The second arm of the blank-field chain, app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:123-127, driven through its LOW-VALUES half. WHEN PASSWDI OF COSGN0AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES is a two-term disjunction and the two terms are separately falsifiable: case07 and case08 answer it through SPACES, and this case answers it through LOW-VALUES. Set beside case06, which drives the LOW-VALUES term of the first arm at :118-122, the four cases cover both arms of the chain across both terms of each - which is what the ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :117 requires, and what no smaller set of them can claim.

The path. USERIDI carries USER0004 - the ninth seeded row, zero-based row 8 - so the test at :118 is false and the EVALUATE falls through to :123, which matches because the password arrives as eight X'00' bytes. :124 moves 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG, :125 moves 'Please enter Password ...' into WS-MESSAGE, :126 moves -1 into PASSWDL rather than USERIDL, and :127 performs SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN. The key typed is deliberately a 'U'-type user where case08 typed the 'A'-type ADMIN004: neither blank-field arm consults SEC-USR-TYPE, and driving the pair with the two different user types states that positively instead of leaving it to be inferred from one row of seed data.

The password item is declared explicitly at eight X'00' bytes rather than omitted, and X'00' is emphatically not X'20'. Omitting the member would arrive at the same image, because an absent field is read as LOW-VALUES at its declared width, but only the explicit form states on the page which of the two terms this case exists to drive - and it is the same convention case01 and case06 use, so the marker reads identically everywhere in this folder. The distinction is what makes the two terms independently falsifiable. A translation testing String.isBlank() would report eight X'00' as non-blank, miss this arm, fall through to WHEN OTHER at :128-129 and use the nulls as a password, answering 'Wrong Password. Try again ...' from :242-243 instead of 'Please enter Password ...' from :125; one testing trim().isEmpty() would pass here and still be wrong, because it would also report a field mixing spaces and nulls as blank where the COBOL treats it as data. SignOnService settles it by comparing the image against spaces of its width and against low-values of its width, and against nothing else.

What :132-136 do on a rejected path, and the read that does not happen. Those lines sit after END-EVALUATE at :130 and outside every arm of it, so they run unconditionally. :132-134 moves FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI) into both WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID, so the communication area carries USER0004 on a rejected sign-on. :135-136 moves FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(PASSWDI) into WS-USER-PWD - and FUNCTION UPPER-CASE alters only lower-case alphabetics, passing every other byte through untouched, so eight X'00' bytes fold to eight X'00' bytes and WS-USER-PWD holds LOW-VALUES rather than spaces. That is the one substantive difference between this case and its SPACES twin case08, where the very same unconditional move yields eight spaces; quietly normalising the nulls to spaces, or folding the normalisation into the success path, would each show up here as a diff. Only then does :138 test the 88-level ERR-FLG-ON, find it on, and skip READ-USER-SEC-FILE.

USRSEC is therefore read exactly zero times, and that is the sharpest point of this case. All ten rows are seeded, every one of them stays unread, no SEC-USR-* value appears anywhere in the outcome because no record was ever returned, and the expectedFinalState images are the seeded rows unchanged. USER0004 is a real, resolvable key: a translation that looked it up because it had a valid key to hand would paint exactly the right screen and would satisfy every other expectation declared here, yet the COBOL never issues the read, because :138 was already decided by :124. For the same reason CDEMO-USER-TYPE stays blank - it is written only at :227, on the path where :223 compared the passwords equal - and it must not read 'U' merely because USER0004 happens to be a regular user in the seed data. CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT are written at :224-228 on that same path and are likewise untouched here.

The screen. This path never executes MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COSGN0AO - that is :81, on the cold start where EIBCALEN is zero - and app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:85 declares 01 COSGN0AO REDEFINES COSGN0AI, where each field's input view spends xxxL plus xxxF plus a four-byte FILLER, seven bytes, exactly where the output view spends a three-byte FILLER plus xxxC, xxxP, xxxH and xxxV. xxxI and xxxO are therefore the same bytes at the same width, so what RECEIVE MAP left there is what SEND MAP transmits: USERIDO is USER0004 and PASSWDO is the eight X'00' bytes that arrived, passed straight through. ERRMSGO is 'Please enter Password ...', twenty-five characters - one more than the twenty-four of the user-id message, which is why the two arms cannot be told apart by length alone - right-padded to the PIC X(78) that app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:152 declares, the width at which the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE of :38 loses its last two bytes. Three absences are stated rather than left to be rediscovered. :59 reads *COPY DFHATTR., an asterisk in column 7 and so a COBOL comment, which means no DFHATTR attribute constant applies to this program at all. COSGN00C never copies CSSETATY - its only consumer is COACTUPC - so there is no DFHRED-plus-'*' emphasis applied at run time, which is why attributes is empty by derivation and not by omission; the error is emphasised by the PASSWDL cursor request together with ERRMSG's static COLOR=RED and ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) at app/bms/COSGN00.bms:197-200. And PASSWD is statically ATTRB=(DRK,FSET,UNPROT) at app/bms/COSGN00.bms:175-180 - a dark, non-display field - which is a property of the map rather than something the program sets, and which is why eight bytes the terminal never showed travel back in a field it never displays. The cursor itself is response metadata and never a payload member: MOVE -1 TO PASSWDL is an instruction to CICS rather than data, so it is carried as cursorField PASSWDL and the xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items appear nowhere among the fields. No USERIDL request is made, because :126 is the only MOVE -1 on this path.

USRSEC is seeded from app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose ten in-stream rows are 57 characters where app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy declares 80: SEC-USR-ID X(08) at 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 - which is 57 - then SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, which is 80. The 23-byte shortfall is supplied once at seed time by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation and never hand-padded, and the 80-character expectedFinalState images prove that span was emitted as 23 spaces - a record missing it would be short by exactly 23. SEC-USR-FILLER is a named data item whose name merely contains the word FILLER, not COBOL's anonymous FILLER. The same job corroborates the target width twice, with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) on SYSUT2 and RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) on the cluster. The dataset is addressed by its binding key USRSEC - the CICS file name at :39 - and never by a dataset name. Every seeded password is the literal PASSWORD, eight characters filling PIC X(08) with no padding, and it stays plaintext because :223 compares it in plaintext; transforming that span in any way would change observable behaviour. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion: COSGN00C contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE on any path, and the read at :211-219 does not even specify UPDATE, so it takes no lock and holds no record. expectedReturnCode is 0 because grep -c RETURN-CODE over the program is 0, and expectedMessages is empty because grep -c DISPLAY over it is 0 too - the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE is observable here only as its 78-byte ERRMSGO projection.

Determinism and the two substitutions. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO opens with MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CURDATE-DATA at :179, so the clock is pinned rather than read: 2022-07-19T23:12:33, traceable to this program's own version footer at :259 and expressed as a fixed local date-time so no timezone can shift it. Through app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY is MM '/' DD '/' YY with YY taken from WS-CURDATE-YEAR(3:2), giving CURDATEO exactly 07/19/22 at its PIC X(8); WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS is HH ':' MM ':' SS, eight bytes, moved into CURTIMEO which app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:122 declares PIC X(9) - hence 23:12:33 followed by exactly one trailing space. Note that width: the sibling COUSR02 map declares its CURTIMEO PIC X(8) and the two must not be conflated. APPLID and SYSID come from EXEC CICS ASSIGN at :198-204, which has no Java equivalent and which neither application.yml nor application-test.yml binds, so CICSAWS1 and AWS1 space-padded to PIC X(8) are pinned constants standing in for those two calls; all twenty cases use the same pair, and the substitution is stated rather than hidden. The charset is named explicitly as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default, which is the classic way a fixed-width expectation silently stops meaning what it says.

Provenance. Every expected value above is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record layout, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the communication area, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy and app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy and app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the literals and the header, app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY with app/bms/COSGN00.bms for the screen field shapes, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:378-379 for transaction CC00, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten seed rows. It was never captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand.

The unit is SignOnService, driven as a plain object with a fixture-backed SecUserRepository, and the eleven-field screen is projected by SignOnController, also a plain object - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path. All conversation state travels in the payload, so no server-side session exists to hold any of it, and this case is one of the re-entry halves of the ENTER/REENTER pair: EIBCALEN is 160, so :80 is false and :85 evaluates EIBAID. Neither the backward-GO TO restructuring gate nor the abend gate applies: grep -c "GO TO" and grep -c CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl are both 0, and neither is faked. The file-status gate is not exercised either, because no file operation occurs on this path at all - which is the whole point of the case - and it is recorded as not exercised rather than satisfied by a fabricated read.
